```{python}
    called from a nuclear stain outward, so a long tail here is cytoplasmic signal being
    attached to a nucleus some distance away — which is what nucleus_ratio sees per cell,
    seen per molecule. It is log-count because the mode at zero (transcripts inside a
    nucleus) is orders of magnitude taller than the tail that carries the information.

    The nucleus-overlap panel is the same question reduced to a fraction, kept because
    that single number is what gets compared between samples.
    """
    display(Markdown("## Transcript placement"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Left, the distribution of transcripts through the imaged z-planes. Middle, each "
        "transcript's distance to its nucleus, with counts on a log axis. Right, the share "
        "of transcripts falling inside a nucleus against outside one."
    ))

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)

    ax = axes[0, 0]
    ax.hist(tx["z"].to_numpy(dtype=float), bins=60,
            color=BAR_FILL, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.25)
    ax.set_xlabel("z (µm)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Transcripts")

    ax = axes[0, 1]
    ax.hist(tx["nucleus_distance"].to_numpy(dtype=float), bins=60,
            color=BAR_FILL, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.25)
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel("Distance to nucleus (µm)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Transcripts")

    ax = axes[0, 2]
    # uint8 0/1 out of the reader, named here so the axis is readable without the schema.
    overlap = tx["overlaps_nucleus"].to_numpy()
    shares = [float((overlap == 0).mean()), float((overlap == 1).mean())]
    ax.bar([0, 1], shares, color=BAR_FILL, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.25)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_xticklabels(["Outside\nnucleus", "Inside\nnucleus"], fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("Share of transcripts")
    for i, share in enumerate(shares):
        ax.annotate(f"{share:.1%}", xy=(i, share), ha="center",
                    xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points",
                    color=ANNOTATION_INK, fontsize=7.5)

    for ax in axes.ravel():
        ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID_INK, lw=0.6)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)
        ax.tick_params(length=0)
        ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)

    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(tx):,} transcripts", x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
```

```{python}
# One `# <sample>` section per sample, driven by the staged zarrs rather than a hardcoded
# block each: the cohort changes, and a hardcoded list silently omits a new sample while
# raising KeyError on a removed one.
#
# Each sample's AnnData is dropped as soon as its slides are drawn, so a cohort's worth
# of obs frames is never co-resident.
#
# Every heading here and in the slide functions is emitted with display(Markdown(...))
# from an ORDINARY cell, NOT under `output: asis`. Under asis everything a cell displays
# concatenates into one raw markdown stream: the figure lands between the blocks and
# leaves the next heading not starting its own line, so pandoc prints a literal "## ..."
# as text and drops the image entirely. display(Markdown) does not hit it — each call
# emits its own complete block, and each figure ends with plt.show() so it lands
# between them.
for path in ZARRS:
    # Load the sample as one SpatialData and hand that to every slide, reaching for
    # .tables["table"] where a slide wants the annotations. One object, loaded once, in
    # the pipeline's own artifact type — no second representation to keep in step.
    #
    # Labels, tables and points: the deck draws the segmentation, reads obs and var, and
    # aggregates the molecule table. Images stay out because it plots none of them.
    #
    # Points come back as a lazy Dask frame and cost nothing until asked; the one
    # materialization is TX_COLUMNS below.
    #
    # This does read X into memory, which the previous read_lazy loader avoided. The
    # trade is worth it — 17 MB for a 21k-cell ROI, and the lazy version needed
    # adata.obs/var .to_memory() calls anyway, because read_lazy returns them as xarray
    # Dataset2D and every scanpy/squidpy plot fails on that (scverse/anndata#981).
    # Loading plainly costs some memory and removes a workaround. Revisit if a cohort of
    # whole-slide samples makes X the binding constraint; it is per sample and dropped
    # below, so the ceiling is one sample's matrix, not the cohort's.
    sdata = spatialdata.read_zarr(path, selection=("labels", "tables", "points"))
    table = sdata.tables["table"]

    # This deck computes no PER-CELL or PER-GENE metric of its own, and has no fallbacks.
    # A report that derives such a metric is a second definition of it, and the two drift
    # without anything saying so; a fallback is that second definition wearing a disguise,
    # letting a stale cohort render a deck whose numbers came from outside the pipeline.
    # Failing here names the fix, which is to re-run create_sdata.
    #
    # The molecule-level slides ARE the exception, and it is a deliberate one. qv,
    # codeword category, field of view and nucleus placement are properties of the
    # transcript table, not summaries of X, so create_sdata never computed them and there
    # is no pipeline definition for this deck to contradict — the rule exists to stop two
    # definitions of one metric, and here there is only one. They are aggregated straight
    # off points below. If any of them later earns a place in create_sdata's uns, this
    # deck should read it from there and this exception should shrink.
    #
    # Outside the per-sample try below, deliberately: a missing column means the whole
    # cohort came from a create_sdata that predates it, so failing the render outright is
    # more useful than a traceback slide repeated once per sample.
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_OBS if c not in table.obs.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{Path(path).name}: obs is missing {missing}. These come from create_sdata "
            "— re-run it over this sample rather than deriving them here."
        )
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_VAR if c not in table.var.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{Path(path).name}: var is missing {missing}. These come from create_sdata "
            "— re-run it over this sample rather than deriving them here."
        )

    # obs["sample"] is written by create_sdata, so the sample id comes from the object
    # rather than the staged path — which is a meaningless sample1.zarr, since the
    # process stages every zarr under an indexed name.
    sample = str(table.obs["sample"].iloc[0])

    display(Markdown(f"# {sample}"))

    # The slides, in the order they appear, each caught independently. Built from METRICS
    # rather than written out, so a metric added there appears on all three plot types at
    # once and nothing can be added to one and forgotten on another: the histogram grids
    # in chunks of HIST_PANELS, then the scatter and the tissue panel once per metric.
    #
    # The scatter skips the categorical metric only because sc.pl.scatter is the one call
    # here whose colour handling this deck does not control; every numeric metric gets all
    # three views, including the two that ARE the scatter's axes — see that slide's
    # docstring for why the degenerate colours are kept rather than filtered out.
    slides = []
    # Retention first: it is the answer the deck exists to give, and the distributions
    # below are the context for reading it.
    if "retention" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [retention_slide]
    if "cell_distributions" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [partial(qc_histogram_slide,
                           metrics=CELL_HIST_METRICS[i:i + HIST_PANELS])
                   for i in range(0, len(CELL_HIST_METRICS), HIST_PANELS)]
    if "cell_scatter" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [partial(transcripts_vs_genes_slide, color=col, label=label,
                           vmax=vmax)
                   for col, label, vmax in SCATTER_METRICS]
    if "cell_tissue" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [partial(qc_tissue_labels_slide, color=col, label=label, scale=scale)
                   for col, label, scale in TISSUE_METRICS]

    # The gene→category lookup is READ from var, where create_sdata annotated it, rather
    # than rebuilt from the molecule table. The deck used to derive it here, and that was
    # its last remaining reason to materialize 7M rows on a default render.
    #
    # Normalised to object/None on the way in rather than trusted. create_sdata writes it
    # that way, but a zarr round-trip can return the column as a categorical or a nullable
    # string, and pd.NA == "predesigned_gene" evaluates to pd.NA rather than False — which
    # makes every comparison-built mask downstream raise "boolean value of NA is ambiguous"
    # instead of simply excluding the gene. This is a dtype normalisation, not a second
    # definition of the value: an unmapped gene stays unmapped and the slides name it.
    gene_category = table.var["codeword_category"]
    gene_category = gene_category.astype(object).where(gene_category.notna(), None)

    # The molecule table is materialized ONLY for the sections that plot it. Nothing above
    # this point needs it any more, so a default render — where both molecule sections are
    # off — never touches points at all.
    #
    # It is the one materialization in this deck and the only shared state its slides read,
    # so it gets its own try: if it fails, every molecule slide is meaningless and they are
    # skipped together rather than each repeating the same traceback. That is the case the
    # per-slide catch below explicitly does not cover. The gene slides are unaffected now
    # that their colouring comes from var.
    #
    # Only TX_COLUMNS, never the whole frame — the table carries coordinates and ids this
    # deck does not plot, and they are most of its width. ~7M rows for a 21k-cell ROI takes
    # about a second. A whole-slide sample is where this becomes the binding constraint,
    # and the fix there is to aggregate lazily in Dask (value_counts and groupby both
    # support it) rather than to materialize and subsample.
    tx = None
    if SECTIONS & {"transcript_stats", "molecule_maps"}:
        try:
            tx = sdata.points["transcripts"][TX_COLUMNS].compute()
        except Exception:
            display(Markdown("## Transcript-level QC"))
            display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    # Then the gene side, reading var, and finally the molecule side, reading points. The
    # order is cells, genes, transcripts — widest unit to narrowest, so each section is a
    # finer-grained account of the same sample rather than an unrelated appendix.
    if "gene_distributions" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [partial(qc_histogram_slide, metrics=GENE_HIST_METRICS, level="var"),
                   partial(gene_rank_slide, gene_category=gene_category),
                   partial(gene_detection_slide, gene_category=gene_category),
                   partial(undetected_genes_slide, gene_category=gene_category)]

    if tx is not None and "transcript_stats" in SECTIONS:
        slides += [partial(transcript_qv_slide, tx=tx),
                   partial(qv_by_category_slide, tx=tx),
                   partial(codeword_category_slide, tx=tx),
                   partial(transcript_fov_slide, tx=tx),
                   partial(transcript_geometry_slide, tx=tx)]

    if tx is not None and "molecule_maps" in SECTIONS:
        # The molecule maps: the whole table first, as the reference the subsets are
        # read against, then one map per subset.
        #
        # Each subset is registered as its own points ELEMENT rather than being selected
        # inside the slide, so every map is the same render_points call over a different
        # element. Filtering a points element preserves its transformations in .attrs, so
        # they must NOT be passed to PointsModel.parse as well — doing both raises
        # "Transformations are both specified for the element and also passed as an
        # argument". Assigning the filtered frame straight back is enough.
        #
        # All of this stays lazy: dask holds the filter and the constant column as
        # unevaluated expressions, so nothing is read until a map is actually drawn.
        points = sdata.points["transcripts"]
        points[MAP_COUNT_COLUMN] = 1.0
        sdata.points["transcripts"] = points
        for element, _, predicate, _, _ in TX_MAPS:
            if predicate is not None:
                sdata.points[element] = points[predicate(points)]

        # How big each subset actually is, as a NUMBER rather than a density to be eyeballed
        # off the map. The share of transcripts assigned to no cell is the one segmentation
        # figure nothing else in the pipeline reports, and reading it off a map is guesswork.
        #
        # One dask.compute over all four, so the subsets share a single pass rather than
        # scanning the table once per map. Counting is far cheaper than the renders that
        # follow, all of which read the same points.
        map_counts = dask.compute(*[sdata.points[element].shape[0]
                                    for element, *_ in TX_MAPS])
        n_all = map_counts[0]

        slides += [partial(transcript_map_slide, element=element, label=label,
                           vmax=vmax, size=size, n_molecules=n,
                           share=(n / n_all if n_all else float("nan")))
                   for (element, label, _, vmax, size), n in zip(TX_MAPS, map_counts)]

    # This loop is a single cell, so anything raising without being caught aborts the cell
    # and drops every LATER sample from the deck too — with the render still exiting 0
    # under `error: true`.
    #
    # Per slide rather than per sample because these slides share nothing: each reads the
    # same adata and draws its own figure, so one failing says nothing about the others.
    # Catching
    # here also puts the traceback under the failed slide's OWN title, since every slide
    # function emits its heading before it plots — which names the broken slide instead
    # of leaving a traceback loose in the section.
    #
    # (The molecule table above is exactly that case, and is guarded on its own.)
    for slide in slides:
        try:
            slide(sdata, sample)
        except Exception:
            # close(), not close(fig): the slide raised before reaching its own close,
            # so the half-built figure is still open and unreachable from here.
            plt.close()
            display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    # tx is the largest thing here by far, so it is dropped with the rest rather than
    # being left to survive into the next sample's load.
    del sdata, table, tx, gene_category
```
